# The Vault Heist

Mara Vale went down the service stair at dusk, counting each of the 40 steps.
The Undervault waited below the street plate, colder than the maps promised.
She still carried the Kestrel Syndicate mark on her wrist, and she still answered to it.
Joss Arden met her at the second gate, a fixer with a lamp and a short temper.
"You are late," Joss said. "The door watch rotates in 9 minutes."
Mara spread the survey sheets across the crate lid and weighted them with bolts.
The missing map was not among them, and that absence was the whole reason they had come.
Her blue eyes caught the lamplight as she read the vault schedule twice.
"3 seals," she said. "2 of them are older than the charter itself."
Joss cut the first seal while Mara timed the watch lights overhead.
The second seal gave way with a sound like ice leaving a river.
Behind the vault door the shelves stood empty except for a single tube of drawings.
Mara lifted it, read the label, and laughed once, quietly, without any joy in it.
The tube was addressed to her, in her own handwriting, dated 2 years ahead.
They closed the door behind them and left the Undervault darker than they found it.
